clauses.current_legal_basis: The ordering lead of EO 10431 continues because the order states no end and the searches checked through 2026-10-14 found no instrument revoking it; the only later instrument found changes other items and the 1953 implementing regulations, not the order's continuation.
clauses.reason: The ordering lead recites the President's authority as President and Commander in Chief and directs the numbered items; it states no end and no held later instrument revokes the order, so it remains in force on 2026-10-14 with the items it introduces.

clauses.current_legal_basis: The establishment of the National Security Medal in item 1 continues because no end is stated and no held instrument changed item 1; the U.S. Code, eCFR and Office of the Federal Register searches checked through 2026-10-14 show no revocation.
clauses.reason: Item 1 establishes the National Security Medal with ribbons and appurtenances and has the design approved by the Executive Secretary of the National Security Council. It states no end, and no held later instrument revokes or amends item 1, so item 1 is operative on 2026-10-14.

clauses.current_legal_basis: Item 2, as amended by Executive Order 13709 section 1(a), continues because the amendment rewrites the eligibility standard rather than ending it and no instrument ends EO 10431 in the searches checked through 2026-10-14.
clauses.reason: Item 2 as issued in 1953 allowed the medal to be awarded to any person, without regard to nationality, including members of the armed forces, for distinguished achievement or outstanding contribution on or after July 26, 1947 in the field of intelligence relating to the national security. Executive Order 13709 section 1(a) (80 FR 60793, effective on signing, October 2, 2015) amended section 2 'to read as follows', widening the field to national security and limiting the award to exceptionally meritorious service in a position of high responsibility or an act of heroism; this changes the substance of item 2 and is a note for the human reviewer. Under the strike-and-insert ruling the clause continues, amended, until the parent order ends; the parent has not been revoked, so item 2 is operative as amended on 2026-10-14.

clauses.current_legal_basis: Item 3's award authority continues because Executive Order 13709 section 2 supersedes only the 1953 implementing regulations, not the order, and no instrument revokes EO 10431 in the searches checked through 2026-10-14.

later_events.mechanism: supersession of the 1953 implementing regulations (not of this clause)

clauses.reason: Item 3 provides that the President, or under regulations approved by the President such person or persons as the President designates, awards the decoration. Executive Order 13709 section 2 supersedes the regulations governing the award issued with Presidential approval on January 19, 1953 and published with Executive Order 10431; that supersedes those regulations only and does not extinguish item 3, whose delegation is in terms of regulations approved by the President from time to time. Item 3 is operative on 2026-10-14. Executive Order 13709 is listed as a later event so that the supersession of the implementing regulations is disclosed.

clauses.current_legal_basis: The one-medal rule and device provision in item 4 continue because no end is stated, no held instrument changed it and the searches checked through 2026-10-14 show no revocation.
clauses.reason: Item 4 limits each person to one National Security Medal, with a suitable device for subsequent services justifying an award. It states no end, no held instrument amends or revokes it, so it is operative on 2026-10-14.

clauses.current_legal_basis: The authority to wear the medal and ribbon in item 5 continues because no end is stated, no held instrument changed it and the searches checked through 2026-10-14 show no revocation.
clauses.reason: Item 5 authorizes armed forces members awarded the decoration to wear the medal and ribbon as authorized by uniform regulations approved by the Secretary of Defense. It states no end, no held instrument amends or revokes it, so it is operative on 2026-10-14.

clauses.current_legal_basis: The posthumous-award permission in item 6 continues because no end is stated, no held instrument changed it and the searches checked through 2026-10-14 show no revocation.
clauses.reason: Item 6 provides that the decoration may be awarded posthumously. It states no end, no held instrument amends or revokes it, so it is operative on 2026-10-14.

conflict_resolutions.PARTIAL_END_CANDIDATE_ON_YES_ORDER: The three supersession candidates all come from section 2 of Executive Order 13709, which supersedes the regulations governing the award of the National Security Medal that were issued with Presidential approval on January 19, 1953 and published with Executive Order 10431. Those regulations are a separate implementing text, not one of the order's seven clauses, and the section does not say that it revokes or supersedes Executive Order 10431 or any of its items; the same order's section 1 amends item 2 and adds items 7 and 8 of Executive Order 10431, which presupposes that the order continues. No clause is therefore ended; item 2 is recorded as amended and item 3 discloses the supersession of the regulations it refers to.

research_rationale:
Read the held Federal Register text of EO 10431 (18 FR 437, 3 CFR 1949-1953 Comp. p. 927; jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10431.txt) in full. It establishes the National Security Medal and has an ordering lead and six numbered items. The prepared inventory omitted item 4 because the OCR reads its number as '4 -', so the inventory is corrected by characters to seven clauses (lead and items 1 to 6). The held Federal Register text of Executive Order 13709 (80 FR 60793, October 7, 2015) is the only later instrument found: section 1(a) rewrites item 2, section 1(b) adds items 7 and 8, and section 2 supersedes the 1953 regulations published with the order; none of them revokes or supersedes the order itself. The three bounded machine searches (U.S. Code through 2026-10-09, eCFR as of 2026-10-14, Office of the Federal Register disposition notes) were read; their hits for this order are leads (the Executive Order 13709 amendment and later citations) and no instrument is shown ending the order. The held-corpus number search finds the order, its 1989 codification SOURCE line, the American Presidency Project and Federal Register copies of Executive Order 13709. Every item is therefore operative on 2026-10-14 under the held original plus bounded search route, item 2 as amended. Limits: the U.S. Code search does not reflect laws enacted from 2026-10-10 through 2026-10-14; the text is the OCR layer of the official page.

savings.reason: EO 10431 has no savings or transitional provision. Medals already awarded under it are not undone by any held later instrument; Executive Order 13709 changes eligibility prospectively only in its own terms.
